title: Extract Action Items from Multi-Party Email Threads
description:
At a project management company, teams drown in email threads. Your pipeline receives raw email thread text (multiple participants, replies, forwards, quoted text) and must extract:

1. A **summary** (2-3 sentences capturing the thread's purpose and outcome)
2. All **action_items** — each with: assignee, task, deadline (if mentioned, else null), priority (high/medium/low), status (new/in_progress/blocked/done)
3. All **decisions_made** — each with: decision, decided_by, date
4. **open_questions** — unresolved questions that still need answers

Output a JSON object to stdout with keys: summary, action_items, decisions_made, open_questions.

The hard part: emails are messy. People reply inline, change subjects mid-thread, delegate vaguely ('can someone handle this?'), reference previous conversations, and use ambiguous pronouns. Your prompt engineering must handle all of this.
company_context: Companies like Asana, Monday.com, and Notion are building AI features to extract action items from communication channels. Engineers who built Superhuman's AI triage report that accurately identifying ownership is the hardest part — 'someone should do this' is not an assignment.

sample_input.email_thread:
From: Alice
To: Bob
Subject: Meeting notes

Bob, can you send the Q1 report by Friday?

---
From: Bob
To: Alice

Sure, I'll have it ready by Thursday.

sample_output.summary: Alice requested the Q1 report from Bob, who agreed to deliver by Thursday.

skip_conditions: Auto-generated emails (out-of-office replies, calendar notifications, mailing list digests, automated CI/CD alerts) must be excluded from action item extraction
Forwarded external marketing or newsletter content embedded in the thread must be ignored

Quoted text from PRIOR threads (prefixed with '>' or appearing below '---------- Forwarded message ----------') should only be referenced for context — do NOT extract action items from quoted/forwarded content unless a new participant explicitly re-assigns or re-confirms them
Emails marked [REDACTED] or [CONFIDENTIAL — REMOVED] should be noted as gaps but not fabricated
action_item_rules: Only extract action items with a CLEAR assignee — 'someone should look into this' or 'we need to figure out X' are open_questions, NOT action items
If an action item is REASSIGNED in a later email, only include the FINAL assignment (with the latest assignee)
If an action item is explicitly marked as DONE or COMPLETED in a later email, set its status to 'done'
If an action item is CANCELLED or explicitly stated as no longer needed, exclude it entirely
Distinguish between NEW action items arising from this thread and references to PRE-EXISTING tasks — only include items that are created or modified in THIS thread
decision_rules: A decision requires someone with authority explicitly choosing between options or approving a course of action
Suggestions, proposals, and opinions are NOT decisions unless confirmed/approved by a decision-maker
If a decision is REVERSED in a later email, only include the FINAL decision
date_rules: When relative dates are used (e.g., 'by Friday', 'next Wednesday'), resolve them using the email's send date as reference
Use YYYY-MM-DD format for all dates in output

inputs.email_thread:
From: Jennifer Walsh <j.walsh@meridian.io>
To: Platform Team <platform-team@meridian.io>
Date: Mon, Feb 12 2024 9:14 AM
Subject: [URGENT] Customer data migration — BlueChip account

Team,

BlueChip Industries (our second-largest enterprise client, $2.4M ARR) needs to migrate from our legacy v1 API to v2 by March 15. Their contract renewal is April 1 and they've made this a hard blocker for renewal.

Here's what we know:
- They have ~3.2 million records across 47 workspaces
- Their data includes custom fields that don't have v2 equivalents yet
- They've already attempted the self-serve migration tool and it failed at 73% (same bug as Acme Corp last month?)
- Their IT team is available for calls Tues/Thurs 2-4 PM EST

@David — can you look into the migration tool failure? This might be the same issue Sarah P. patched for Acme.
@Ravi — we need a mapping spec for their custom fields to v2 equivalents. Can you have a draft by Wednesday?
@Lisa — please schedule a kickoff call with their IT team for this Thursday.

I'll set up a war room Slack channel and we'll do daily standups at 9:30 AM starting tomorrow.

This is top priority for the next 4 weeks. Let me know if you have any conflicts.

Jen

---
From: David Kim <d.kim@meridian.io>
To: Platform Team <platform-team@meridian.io>
Date: Mon, Feb 12 2024 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Customer data migration — BlueChip account

Jen,

Just checked — it's NOT the same bug as Acme. That was a UTF-8 encoding issue with Japanese characters. BlueChip's failure is different: their workspace "BlueChip-Analytics" has records with attachment references pointing to our deprecated blob storage (pre-2022 data). The migration tool doesn't know how to handle those references.

Two options:
1. Build a shim that maps old blob URLs to our new CDN paths (2-3 days of work)
2. Export the attachments separately and have BlueChip's team re-upload (puts burden on them)

I'd recommend option 1 but I need Ravi's input on whether there are other deprecated storage references we should handle at the same time.

Also — I'm on PTO Thursday-Friday this week. Can someone cover the Thursday standup?

- David

---
From: Ravi Mehta <r.mehta@meridian.io>
To: Platform Team <platform-team@meridian.io>
Date: Mon, Feb 12 2024 11:30 AM
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Customer data migration — BlueChip account

@David — agreed on option 1. There are actually 3 types of deprecated storage refs:
1. Pre-2022 blob storage (what you found)
2. Legacy "embedded files" from v0 API (very rare, but BlueChip was an early adopter)
3. S3 presigned URLs that have long since expired

If we're building a shim, we should handle all three. I can spec this out by tomorrow EOD.

Re: custom fields — I pulled their schema and there are 14 custom fields. 11 map cleanly to v2 equivalents. The remaining 3 are:
- "risk_score" (calculated field — no v2 equivalent, we'd need to create a new field type)
- "legacy_ref" (internal ID from their old system — can be stored as metadata)
- "approval_chain" (JSON blob representing a multi-step approval workflow — this is complex)

The "approval_chain" field is the real problem. It's deeply nested and references user IDs from their v1 auth system. We might need a call with their team to figure out the right mapping.

@Jen — for the Wednesday draft, do you want me to include a recommendation on "risk_score" or just document the gap?

---
From: Lisa Park <l.park@meridian.io>
To: Platform Team <platform-team@meridian.io>
Date: Mon, Feb 12 2024 12:45 PM
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Customer data migration — BlueChip account

Thursday kickoff is scheduled: 2:30 PM EST with BlueChip's IT lead (Tom Bradley) and their CTO (Maria Santos). Calendar invite sent to all of you.

@David since you're on PTO Thursday, should I reschedule or can Ravi cover the technical questions?

Also Jen — should we loop in Customer Success? Their CSM (Angela) might have context on what BlueChip considers a dealbreaker vs nice-to-have for the migration.

---
From: Jennifer Walsh <j.walsh@meridian.io>
To: Platform Team <platform-team@meridian.io>
Date: Mon, Feb 12 2024 1:30 PM
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Customer data migration — BlueChip account

Great progress, team. Decisions:

1. We're going with David's Option 1 (build the shim) AND handling all 3 deprecated storage types per Ravi's recommendation.
2. Ravi — yes, include a recommendation on risk_score in the Wednesday doc. Even if we can't solve it perfectly, BlueChip needs to know our plan.
3. Lisa — yes, please add Angela to the Thursday call. Good thinking.
4. @Ravi — since David's on PTO Thursday, can you lead the technical portion of the kickoff call? David, please do a handoff with Ravi before you leave Wednesday.

One more thing: @David, before you go on PTO, can you file a tech debt ticket for the migration tool? The fact that it fails silently at 73% instead of giving a clear error is unacceptable — this is the second customer hit by it.

War room channel created: #proj-bluechip-migration
Daily standup: 9:30 AM starting tomorrow in that channel.

- Jen

---

From: David Kim <d.kim@meridian.io>

Sounds good on all fronts.

Re: handoff — @Ravi can we do a 30-min sync tomorrow (Tues) afternoon? I'll have a draft of the shim architecture by then and can walk you through the blob storage mapping logic. That way you'll be ready for Thursday.

One question for the group: should the shim be a permanent part of the migration tool, or a one-off script specifically for BlueChip? If permanent, the scope is bigger but benefits future customers with legacy data. Thoughts?

---
From: Sarah Patel <s.patel@meridian.io>
To: Platform Team <platform-team@meridian.io>
Date: Mon, Feb 12 2024 2:45 PM
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Customer data migration — BlueChip account

Just chiming in since my name came up re: the Acme fix.

David is right that BlueChip's issue is different from Acme's. But FYI — when I patched the UTF-8 bug, I noticed the migration tool also doesn't handle records with more than 50 custom fields gracefully. It doesn't crash, but it silently drops fields beyond 50. BlueChip has 14 custom fields so they should be fine, but worth noting for the tech debt ticket.

@David — can you add that to ENG-4421? Or should I file a separate ticket?

From: David Kim <d.kim@meridian.io>
To: Platform Team <platform-team@meridian.io>
Date: Mon, Feb 12 2024 3:10 PM

@Sarah — good catch. I'll add the 50-field limit issue to ENG-4421 since it's related to the same "silent failure" theme. Thanks for flagging.

@Ravi — confirmed for tomorrow 2 PM for the handoff sync.

Subject: Re: [URGENT] Customer data migration — BlueChip account

Team — forwarding Tom Bradley's email with Maria Santos's concerns (see above). Key things we need to address before Thursday:

1. Zero data loss guarantee — @Ravi, can we commit to this?
2. Rollback plan — @David, can you outline a rollback strategy in your shim design?
3. v1 API consumer compatibility — we should probably discuss this at the kickoff

Also good news: Maria says procurement may extend renewal deadline to April 15 if we provide a concrete timeline Thursday. That gives us 2 more weeks.

@Jen — should we update the project timeline given the potential extension?

---
From: Jennifer Walsh <j.walsh@meridian.io>
To: Platform Team <platform-team@meridian.io>
Date: Mon, Feb 12 2024 4:30 PM
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Customer data migration — BlueChip account

Good context from BlueChip, Lisa.

Let's keep March 15 as our internal target regardless of the potential extension — treat the extra 2 weeks as buffer, not as slack.

Decision: @David — yes, please include a rollback strategy in the shim design. Non-negotiable.

@Ravi — re: zero data loss. I think we can commit to zero loss with verification, meaning we run a post-migration validation that compares record counts and checksums. Can you include that in your spec?

We'll address the v1 API consumer question at the Thursday kickoff — that's a BlueChip-side concern and we need their input.

Updated priorities for this week:
- Tues: Ravi delivers storage ref shim spec; David/Ravi handoff sync at 2 PM
- Wed: Ravi delivers custom field mapping doc with risk_score recommendation; David files out for PTO
- Thurs: Kickoff call at 2:30 PM; Ravi leads technical portion
- Fri: Ravi begins shim implementation based on David's architecture

Let's nail this.

- Jen

---
From: Ravi Mehta <r.mehta@meridian.io>
To: Platform Team <platform-team@meridian.io>
Date: Mon, Feb 12 2024 5:00 PM
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Customer data migration — BlueChip account

@David — 2 PM tomorrow works. I'll have my questions ready.

@Jen — agreed on the zero-data-loss-with-verification approach. I'll design a checksum-based validation step into the migration pipeline. Will include in tomorrow's spec.

Re: David's question about permanent vs one-off for the shim — I think permanent is the right call. We have at least 15 other pre-2022 accounts that will eventually hit this same issue when they migrate. Happy to discuss more at standup tomorrow.

Signing off for today — will have the storage ref spec ready by tomorrow 5 PM.

ground_truth.summary: BlueChip Industries ($2.4M ARR) must migrate from v1 to v2 API by March 15 as a hard blocker for their April 1 contract renewal. The migration tool failed due to deprecated blob storage references (not the same bug as Acme). The team decided to build a storage reference shim handling all 3 deprecated types, and identified 3 custom fields without clean v2 equivalents — the most complex being 'approval_chain'. BlueChip's CTO may extend the renewal deadline to April 15 if a concrete timeline is provided by Thursday.

action_items.task: Build shim to map deprecated blob storage URLs to new CDN paths, handling all 3 deprecated storage reference types, with rollback strategy included
File tech debt ticket for migration tool silent failures and add 50-field limit issue
Do technical handoff with Ravi at 2 PM Tuesday
Write custom field mapping spec with recommendation on risk_score field
Deliver deprecated storage reference shim spec with checksum-based validation step
Lead technical portion of Thursday kickoff call with BlueChip
Begin shim implementation based on David's architecture on Friday
Add Angela (CSM) to the Thursday kickoff call
Run daily standups at 9:30 AM in #proj-bluechip-migration starting Tuesday

decisions_made.decision: Build a storage reference shim (Option 1) rather than having BlueChip re-upload, handling all 3 deprecated storage types
Include risk_score recommendation in the Wednesday custom field mapping doc
Add Angela (Customer Success Manager) to the Thursday kickoff call
Ravi will lead technical discussion at Thursday kickoff since David is on PTO
Include rollback strategy in the shim design — non-negotiable
Commit to zero data loss with checksum-based post-migration verification
Keep March 15 as internal target regardless of potential April 15 extension

open_questions: How should the 'approval_chain' custom field (nested JSON with v1 user IDs) be mapped to v2? Needs discussion with BlueChip's team.
Should 'risk_score' calculated field require a new v2 field type, or is there a workaround?
What does BlueChip consider a dealbreaker vs nice-to-have for the migration?
Should the storage reference shim be permanent (in the migration tool) or a one-off script for BlueChip? Team leaning permanent but not finalized.
How will BlueChip's 12 internal tools consuming the v1 API be handled during/after migration?
